scenario: 面试题:设计一个同时处理文本/图像/视频/音频的内容审核数据管线,政策每周还在变。
scenario_en: Interview prompt: design a content-moderation data pipeline handling text/image/video/audio at once, with policies changing weekly.
q: 内容审核的数据策略该围绕哪三大支柱来搭？
q_en: What three pillars should a content-moderation data strategy be built around?
why: 三大支柱:(1)多模态信号当互补证据、每个模态独立提取;(2)policy-aware 标注配可测的质量闸门(IAA);(3)主动学习闭环持续追上演进的政策。数据策略决定模型质量的天花板,先讲它再讲架构。
why_en: Three pillars: multimodal signals as complementary evidence, policy-aware annotation with measurable quality gates, and an active-learning loop that keeps up with evolving policy — the data strategy sets the model's ceiling.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1. 多模态信号
互补证据"] --> C["性能天花板"] B["2. policy-aware 标注
IAA 质量闸门"] --> C D["3. 主动学习闭环
追上政策演进"] --> C C --> E["下一课:分层集成架构"]
options: (1)选最强单模态分类器 (2)堆更大的模型 (3)加更多 GPU
(1)先定 SLA 延迟预算 (2)选向量数据库做相似检索 (3)配置 CDN 分发+多区域灾备
(1)多模态互补信号 (2)policy-aware 标注+IAA 闸门 (3)主动学习闭环
(1)选云厂商 (2)设计前端审核后台 (3)接入支付风控
options_en: (1) pick the strongest single-modality classifier, (2) use a bigger model, (3) add more GPUs.
(1) fix the SLA latency budget first, (2) choose a vector database for similarity retrieval, (3) configure CDN delivery with multi-region failover.
(1) multimodal complementary signals, (2) policy-aware annotation with IAA quality gates, (3) an active-learning loop.
(1) pick a cloud vendor, (2) design the reviewer console UI, (3) integrate payment risk control.
optionExplanations: 堆模型和 GPU 是架构/算力侧,答不到数据策略;标注噪声再大的模型也救不回来。
延迟、向量库、CDN 是服务层细节,不是决定审核质量天花板的数据策略。
对;互补信号、可测标注质量、主动学习闭环三条正是数据策略的骨架,决定性能上限。
云厂商、后台、支付都是周边工程,不构成审核数据策略的核心支柱。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking models and GPUs is the architecture/compute side and misses the data strategy; no model recovers from noisy labels.
Latency, vector DB, and CDN are serving-layer details, not the data strategy that sets the moderation ceiling.
Correct — complementary signals, measurable label quality, and an active-learning loop are the backbone that caps performance.
Cloud vendor, console, and payments are peripheral engineering, not core pillars of a moderation data strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标注者一致性:不同标注者对同一条内容给出相同标签的程度,当质量闸门用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAA (Inter-Annotator Agreement) measures how consistently different annotators assign the same label to the same item, used as a quality gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型挑出最不确定的样本优先送人工标注,再回炉训练的闭环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Active learning is a loop where the model picks its most uncertain items for human labeling, then retrains on them.

scenario: 候选人拿到审核题,立刻画 per-modality encoder + fusion 框图,完全没谈数据从哪来、怎么标。
scenario_en: A candidate immediately draws per-modality encoder + fusion boxes, never addressing where data comes from or how it's labeled.
q: 为什么要先讲数据策略再讲架构？跳过的代价是什么？
q_en: Why cover data strategy before architecture, and what does skipping it cost?
why: 标注质量是模型质量的天花板——标签有噪声,再精巧的 encoder/fusion 也补不回来。直接跳架构是这类题的典型 junior 信号:漂亮框图建在没校准的标签地基上。
why_en: Label quality is the ceiling on model quality, so no encoder or fusion recovers from noisy labels, and jumping to architecture is the classic junior signal.
options: 标注质量是模型质量的天花板,噪声标签架构补不回来
先画架构更高效,数据策略可以在训练阶段再补齐,不影响最终精度
数据策略只跟合规有关,和模型精度无关,面试可略过
架构图漂亮就能过,评委不看数据从哪来
options_en: Label quality caps model quality, and architecture can't recover from noisy labels.
Drawing the architecture first is more efficient; data strategy can be patched during training with no effect on final accuracy.
Data strategy only concerns compliance, is unrelated to model accuracy, and can be skipped in the interview.
A pretty architecture diagram is enough to pass; reviewers don't care where the data comes from.
optionExplanations: 对;标签定天花板,噪声进来模型学的就是噪声,先钉数据策略才让架构有意义。
数据策略定标签口径和质量闸门,训练时再补往往要大批返工,不是无痛可延后项。
标注一致性、soft label 直接决定校准和精度,把它当纯合规问题是误解。
对着劣质标签的漂亮架构就是白费,评委恰恰在看你懂不懂数据是地基。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — labels set the ceiling, so noise in means the model learns noise; pin the data strategy first to make architecture meaningful.
Data strategy fixes label definitions and quality gates; patching later usually forces large-scale rework, not a painless deferral.
Annotation consistency and soft labels directly drive calibration and accuracy, so treating it as pure compliance is a misread.
A pretty architecture over bad labels is wasted, and reviewers are precisely checking whether you see data as the foundation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标注规则直接编码平台政策(什么算违规),而不是靠标注者主观感觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Policy-aware annotation encodes platform policy (what counts as a violation) into the labeling rules rather than annotator gut feel.

scenario: 一个 meme 配了无害文字+暴力图像;一个视频画面正常但音频是仇恨言论。这类内容能骗过任一单模态分类器。
scenario_en: A meme pairs benign text with a violent image; a video shows innocuous visuals but hate-speech audio — both slip past any single-modality classifier.
q: 面对这种跨模态攻击,该怎么组织信号,而不是只上最强的文本分类器？
q_en: Against such cross-modal attacks, how should signals be organized instead of just the strongest text classifier?
why: 跨模态攻击专钻单一信号的盲区:文本干净就把恶意塞进图像/音频。设计原则是 signal complementarity——文本/图像/视频/音频四个信号各自独立提取,融合前互为补充,任一模态被绕过还有其他三个兜底。
why_en: Cross-modal attacks exploit any single signal's blind spot, so the principle is signal complementarity: extract all four modalities independently as complementary evidence so evading one still leaves three.
tradeoff: 多模态互补(覆盖跨模态攻击但更贵) vs 单一最强模态(便宜但有盲区可被绕过)
options: 只保留最强的文本分类器,图像/音频靠事后人工抽查补,省下三套编码器
四个模态信号各自独立提取、互为补充证据,任一被绕过仍有其他三个兜底
把四个模态拼成一张大图喂给一个图像模型,省掉多编码器
只在文本可疑时才去看图像,平时不跑图像/音频
options_en: Keep only the strongest text classifier and cover image/audio with after-the-fact human spot-checks, saving three encoders.
Extract all four modality signals independently as complementary evidence, so evading one still leaves three as backup.
Stitch the four modalities into one big image and feed a single image model, dropping the multi-encoder setup.
Only look at the image when text is suspicious, and otherwise never run image/audio.
whenOtherWins: 若平台本质上是纯文本(如短信/纯文字论坛),没有图像/音视频承载攻击面,单模态文本分类器就够,多模态是过度工程。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform is inherently text-only (SMS, a text-only forum) with no image/AV attack surface, a single-modality text classifier suffices and multimodal is over-engineering.
optionExplanations: 事后抽查覆盖不了实时规模,恶意图像/音频在被抽到前已经传播,盲区照旧。
对，四个模态各自单独提取信号、彼此互相接应，一个模态被绕过时还有另外三个能兜底，这正是本题的判断依据。
拼图会丢掉音频和时序信息,还把四种语义混成一团,反而更难分辨。
条件触发会漏掉'文本干净、恶意只在图像/音频'这一整类攻击,正中盲区。
optionExplanations_en: Spot-checks can't cover real-time scale; malicious image/audio spreads before being sampled, leaving the blind spot open.
Correct — each modality is scored on its own, and if an attacker slips past one, the other three modalities are still watching — that's the design call here.
Stitching drops audio and temporal information and blends four semantics into one, making it harder to tell apart.
Conditional triggering misses the whole 'clean text, malice only in image/audio' class, hitting the blind spot directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把违规内容藏在某个模态里,同时让其他模态显得无害,以此绕过单模态审核。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-modal attack hides the violation in one modality while keeping others benign to slip past single-modality moderation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 四个模态信号各自独立提取、互相补足,单个模态的盲区由其他模态覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signal complementarity extracts each modality independently so one modality's blind spot is covered by the others.

scenario: 为四个模态各配一个编码器,先要说清每个模态在审核里到底抓什么信号。
scenario_en: Before assigning an encoder per modality, be clear on what moderation signal each modality actually captures.
q: 关于四个模态各自贡献的审核信号,哪些说法是对的？(多选)
q_en: Which statements about each modality's moderation signal are correct? (multiple)
why: 文本抓语义上下文,图像抓暴力/裸露/仇恨符号,视频靠时序抓跨帧动态,音频靠转写+声学特征抓口头仇恨和枪声/尖叫。'单一最强模态就够'与互补原则相悖。
why_en: Text catches slurs/threats plus semantic context; image catches violence/nudity/hate-symbols/manipulated media; video catches cross-frame temporal dynamics; audio uses speech-to-text plus acoustics for gunshots/distress.
options: 文本:抓辱骂/威胁/不实声明,还要判语义上下文——讽刺、反串、counter-speech,贬义 vs 被夺回的用法
视频:靠时序建模抓跨帧的动态——升级的暴力、分步自残,这些单帧看不出来
音频:用 speech-to-text 抓口头仇恨,再用声学特征探测枪声、尖叫、人群噪声
结论:选四个里最强的单一模态就够了,多模态属于过度工程
options_en: Text: catches slurs/threats/misinfo claims, and must judge semantic context — sarcasm, counter-speech, derogatory vs reclaimed usage.
Video: uses temporal modeling to catch cross-frame dynamics — escalating violence, step-by-step self-harm invisible in any single frame.
Audio: uses speech-to-text for spoken hate, plus acoustic features to detect gunshots, distress, crowd noise.
Conclusion: pick the single strongest of the four and you're done; multimodal is over-engineering.
optionExplanations: 对;文本不止匹配脏词,还要看意图与语境,不然会把 counter-speech 误伤。
对;暴力升级、自残步骤是跨帧才现形的,单帧和纯文本都抓不到,必须时序建模。
对;音频有两条线——转写出的口头仇恨,和声学层的枪声/尖叫危险信号。
错;单模态有盲区、可被跨模态攻击绕过,互补原则正是要四个都保留。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — text does more than match slurs; it must read intent and context or it will wrongly flag counter-speech.
Correct — escalating violence and self-harm steps only emerge across frames, missed by a single frame or text, so temporal modeling is required.
Correct — audio has two lines: transcribed spoken hate, and acoustic-layer danger signals like gunshots/distress.
Wrong — a single modality has blind spots exploitable by cross-modal attacks; complementarity is exactly why all four are kept.

termDefinitions.meaning: 引用或反驳仇恨言论来反对它的内容;审核要避免把它误判成仇恨本身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counter-speech quotes or rebuts hateful content to oppose it; moderation must avoid flagging it as hate itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被 P 图/深伪等手段改动过的图像视频,纯文本看不出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Manipulated media is imagery altered by editing or deepfakes, invisible to text-only signals.

scenario: 视频审核要采样帧喂给时序模型,算力有限,不可能每帧都跑重编码器。
scenario_en: Video moderation samples frames for a temporal model, but compute is limited and running a heavy encoder on every frame is impossible.
q: 均匀关键帧采样 vs 场景切换采样,核心在权衡什么？
q_en: Uniform key-frame vs scene-change frame sampling — what's the core tradeoff?
why: 均匀关键帧(如每秒 1 帧)实现简单、覆盖稳定,但可能漏掉两帧之间的瞬时违规;场景切换采样在画面变化处才取帧,同样算力下抓到更多语义转折,但实现复杂、静态长镜头会欠采。核心是覆盖率 vs 算力。
why_en: Uniform key-frame sampling is simple and steady but can miss violations between samples; scene-change sampling captures more semantic shifts at the same compute but is complex and under-samples static shots — coverage vs compute.
tradeoff: 均匀关键帧(简单、覆盖稳定但漏瞬时) vs 场景切换(抓语义转折但实现复杂、长镜头欠采)
options: 两种采样精度完全一样,只是代码写法不同
均匀采样一定更准,场景切换只是多花算力换不到额外覆盖
采样策略只影响存储成本,不影响漏检
覆盖率 vs 算力:均匀简单但漏瞬时,场景切换抓转折但更复杂
options_en: The two have identical accuracy; only the code differs.
Uniform sampling is always more accurate, and scene-change just burns extra compute for no added coverage.
Sampling strategy only affects storage cost, not miss rate.
Coverage vs compute: uniform is simple but misses transient violations, while scene-change catches shifts but is more complex.
optionExplanations: 两者对不同内容各有漏检模式,精度不等价,不是纯写法差异。
均匀在场景变化密集的视频反而漏转折,并非一定更准。
采样直接决定哪些帧被看到,漏检风险随策略变,不只是存储问题。
对;这是覆盖率与算力的经典权衡,按视频类型(动作片 vs 长讲座)选采样。
optionExplanations_en: Each has its own miss pattern on different content, so accuracy isn't equivalent — not a mere coding difference.
On videos with dense scene changes, uniform actually misses transitions, so it isn't always more accurate.
Sampling decides which frames are seen, so miss risk varies with strategy — not just storage.
Correct — a classic coverage-vs-compute tradeoff; pick sampling by content type (action clip vs long lecture).

scenario: 确定了要多模态互补,现在要把 signal complementarity 原则落成具体的提取架构。
scenario_en: Having committed to multimodal complementarity, you now turn the signal-complementarity principle into a concrete extraction architecture.
q: signal complementarity 原则在提取阶段该怎么落地？
q_en: How does the signal-complementarity principle land at the extraction stage?
why: 四个信号在融合之前,由各自独立的 per-modality 编码器分别提取——文本、图像、视频、音频各跑各的,保住每个模态的独立证据。怎么融合是下一课的事;这一阶段的原则就是'先独立提取、后融合'。
why_en: All four signals are extracted by independent per-modality encoders before any fusion, preserving each modality's independent evidence; how to fuse them is the next lesson.
options: 先把四个模态原始数据拼接成一个向量,再交给一个统一编码器学
只训练文本编码器,其余模态用它的输出近似,省掉三个编码器
融合之前,四个模态各由独立编码器分别提取,保住各自证据
先融合成一路信号,融合后再决定要不要拆回各模态
options_en: Concatenate the four raw modalities into one vector first, then let a single unified encoder learn it.
Train only the text encoder and approximate the others from its output, dropping three encoders.
Before fusion, each modality is extracted by its own independent encoder, preserving separate evidence.
Fuse into one signal first, then decide afterward whether to split back into modalities.
optionExplanations: 原始拼接把不同尺度/语义的数据糊在一起,单编码器学不出各模态专门的违规特征。
文本推不出图像里的裸露或音频里的枪声,近似掉三个模态等于丢证据。
对;先独立提取保住每个模态的信号,融合是下一课的事,顺序不能颠倒。
先融合就把独立证据抹平了,再拆回来也拿不回丢掉的模态特异信息。
optionExplanations_en: Raw concatenation blends data of different scales/semantics, so one encoder can't learn each modality's specialized violation features.
Text can't infer nudity in an image or a gunshot in audio, so approximating three modalities throws away evidence.
Correct — extract independently first to preserve each modality's signal; fusion is the next lesson and the order can't be reversed.
Fusing first flattens the independent evidence, and splitting back can't recover the lost modality-specific information.

termDefinitions.term: per-modality encoder / 单模态编码器
termDefinitions.meaning: 为某一个模态(文本/图像/视频/音频)专门训练的编码器,输出该模态的定长嵌入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A per-modality encoder is trained for one modality and outputs a fixed-length embedding of that modality's signal.

scenario: 团队争论:是先投钱堆更大的模型,还是先投钱把标注做干净。
scenario_en: The team debates whether to spend on a bigger model first or on cleaner annotation first.
q: 为什么说'标注质量是模型质量的天花板'？
q_en: Why is 'annotation quality is the ceiling on model quality' true?
why: 模型只能学到标签里的东西:如果同一条内容标注者各标各的、口径不一,模型学到的就是这团噪声,再大的架构也补不回。所以标注一致性设的是上限,不是可后补的细节。
why_en: A model can only learn what the labels encode, so inconsistent noisy labels cap what any architecture can reach, no matter how large.
options: 因为标签定义了模型能学到的上限,噪声标签让再大的架构也补不回来
因为标注只影响训练收敛速度,不影响模型最终能达到的精度上限
因为标注只在冷启动阶段重要,数据一多就无所谓了
因为标注质量只决定推理延迟,与精度无关
options_en: Because labels define the upper bound the model can learn, and noisy labels cap even the largest architecture.
Because annotation only affects training convergence speed, not the final accuracy ceiling the model can reach.
Because annotation only matters at cold start and becomes irrelevant once data is plentiful.
Because annotation quality only decides inference latency, unrelated to accuracy.
optionExplanations: 对;监督学习的目标就是标签,标签一乱,模型的天花板就被钉死在噪声上。
噪声标签改变的是模型能达到的正确率上限,不只是收敛快慢。
数据再多,如果每条都标错口径,量大只会把系统性偏差放大。
标注质量是训练侧的正确性问题,和推理延迟是两码事。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — supervised learning targets the labels, so once labels are messy the ceiling is pinned to the noise.
Noisy labels change the achievable accuracy ceiling, not just how fast training converges.
More data with consistently wrong labels just amplifies the systematic bias at scale.
Label quality is a training-side correctness issue, distinct from inference latency.

scenario: 仇恨言论标注,标注者各凭主观感觉判断,同一条内容标签方差很大,吵起来也说不清谁对。
scenario_en: For hate-speech labeling, annotators judge by subjective feel; the same item gets high label variance and disagreements can't be resolved.
q: 怎么把标注从主观判断变成可复现、可追溯的？
q_en: How do you turn labeling from subjective judgment into something reproducible and traceable?
why: 把纳入/排除规则编码成结构化决策树:是否基于身份的语言? → 贬义/讽刺/counter-speech? → 有没有新闻/教育等语境豁免? 标注者顺着树走而不是凭感觉,方差下降、分歧可追溯到具体节点。
why_en: Encode inclusion/exclusion rules into a structured decision tree (identity-based? derogatory vs satire vs counter-speech? news/education context exclusion?) so annotators follow the tree, cutting variance and making disagreements traceable to a node.
tradeoff: 决策树(方差低、分歧可追溯但要维护规则) vs 主观判断(灵活但方差大、吵不清)
options: 给标注者更高时薪,让他们更认真地凭主观判断
把纳入/排除规则编码成结构化决策树,标注者顺节点走,分歧可追溯
只留最资深一个人标,彻底避免分歧
取消规则,让模型自己在无标签数据上学出违规定义,再反过来指导标注
options_en: Pay annotators more so they judge subjectively but more carefully.
Encode inclusion/exclusion rules into a structured decision tree so annotators walk the nodes and disagreements stay traceable.
Keep only one most-senior annotator to eliminate disagreement entirely.
Drop the rules, let the model learn the violation definition from unlabeled data, and use that to guide annotators.
whenOtherWins: 若是全新、还没成型政策的违规类型(如刚冒头的编码仇恨),硬套决策树可能过早僵化,应先让政策专家判、把判例沉淀成规则再编码成树。
whenOtherWins_en: For a brand-new harm with no settled policy yet, forcing a rigid tree may ossify prematurely — let policy experts judge first, then codify precedents into a tree.
optionExplanations: 再认真的主观判断也没有统一口径,方差来自规则缺失,不是态度问题。
对;决策树把政策编码成可走的流程,把'凭感觉'换成'顺节点',方差和不可追溯一起解决。
单人标注一致但产能极低、且把一个人的偏差变成全局系统偏差。
无监督学不出平台特定的违规定义,反而更没法追溯为什么这么标。
optionExplanations_en: Even careful subjective judgment lacks a shared rubric; the variance comes from missing rules, not attitude.
Correct — a decision tree encodes policy into a walkable flow, replacing gut feel with node-following and fixing both variance and traceability.
One annotator is consistent but tiny in throughput and turns one person's bias into a global systematic bias.
Unsupervised learning can't recover platform-specific violation definitions and makes labels even less traceable.

termDefinitions.term: annotation decision tree / 标注决策树
termDefinitions.meaning: 把'算不算违规'拆成一串是/否节点的结构化流程,标注者按节点走出标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An annotation decision tree breaks 'is this a violation' into a structured chain of yes/no nodes annotators walk to reach a label.

scenario: 要决定标签粒度:只标 violating/safe 二元,还是标 mild/moderate/severe 严重度分级。
scenario_en: You must choose label granularity: binary violating/safe, or a severity scale of mild/moderate/severe.
q: 什么时候值得多花钱上 severity 严重度分级标签？
q_en: When is it worth the extra cost of severity-graded labels?
why: 当你要按严重度做不同处置时:severity 标签能对齐非对称成本框架——severe 自动删除、mild 路由人工复核。但前提是训练数据本身编码了这个区分;二元便宜但把严重度信息全丢了,没法做阈值调优。
why_en: When you want severity-differentiated actions: severity labels align with the asymmetric-cost framework (auto-remove severe, route mild to review), but only if the training data encodes that distinction.
tradeoff: severity 分级(可按严重度调阈值/处置但更贵) vs 二元(便宜但丢严重度、无法阈值调优)
options: 任何类别都无脑上 severity,分级越细模型一定越好
永远只用二元,分级纯属浪费标注预算
当要按严重度分开处置(severe 自动删/mild 送复核)时
只在延迟预算宽松时才上 severity,和处置策略无关
options_en: Always use severity for every category; finer grades always mean a better model.
Always use binary; grading is pure waste of the labeling budget.
When you'll act differently by severity — auto-remove severe, route mild to review.
Only use severity when the latency budget is loose, unrelated to the enforcement policy.
whenOtherWins: 若某类别(如 child safety)任何程度都一律自动删除,没有'按严重度分档处置'的空间,二元标签就够了,分级是多余成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If a category (e.g. child safety) is auto-removed at any level with no severity-differentiated action, binary labels suffice and grading is wasted cost.
optionExplanations: 无脑分级会在不需要分档的类别上白烧标注预算,还稀释了每档的样本量。
二元丢掉严重度,一旦需要对 mild/severe 分开处置就补不回,不是永远够用。
对;severity 的价值在于支撑差异化处置和阈值调优,前提是数据里真有这个区分。
上不上分级由处置策略决定,不由延迟预算决定,选项张冠李戴。
optionExplanations_en: Blind grading burns labeling budget on categories that need no tiers and thins per-tier sample counts.
Binary drops severity, and once you need to act differently on mild vs severe you can't recover it — not always enough.
Correct — severity's value is enabling differentiated action and threshold tuning, provided the data actually encodes the distinction.
Whether to grade is decided by enforcement policy, not the latency budget — a mismatched reason.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏放一条 severe 违规的代价远大于误删一条,处置阈值要按这个不对称来定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asymmetric cost means missing a severe violation costs far more than a false removal, so thresholds are set around that imbalance.

scenario: 要衡量标注一致性,有人主张直接用'两个标注者答案相同的百分比'当指标。
scenario_en: To measure annotation consistency, someone proposes just using 'percent of items where two annotators agree.'
q: 为什么该用 Fleiss' kappa / Krippendorff's alpha 而不是原始百分比一致率？
q_en: Why use Fleiss' kappa / Krippendorff's alpha instead of raw percent agreement?
why: kappa/alpha 会扣掉纯碰运气也一致的部分,得到真正超出随机的一致性;原始百分比在类别不均衡时会虚高——99% 都是 safe 时瞎标也能有 98% 一致,却测不出真实可靠度。
why_en: Kappa/alpha strip out chance agreement for a true signal, while raw percent inflates on skewed categories — 99% safe items can look 98% 'agreed' from random labeling with no real reliability.
tradeoff: kappa/alpha(扣除随机一致、类别不均衡也可信) vs 原始百分比(直观但不均衡时虚高)
options: 原始百分比更好,因为它数值高、汇报好看
两者等价,kappa 只是原始百分比换个公式表达,没有实质差别
该用准确率 accuracy 衡量标注者之间的一致性,它更直观好解释
kappa/alpha 扣除了'碰巧一致'的部分,原始百分比在类别不均衡时虚高
options_en: Raw percent is better because the number is high and looks good in reports.
They're equivalent — kappa is just raw percent expressed with a different formula, no real difference.
Use accuracy to measure agreement between annotators since it's more intuitive to explain.
Kappa/alpha subtract chance agreement, while raw percent inflates on imbalanced categories.
whenOtherWins: 若类别高度均衡、只是想做一个快速 sanity check(不进正式质量闸门),原始百分比看一眼也行,但不能拿它当卡点决定要不要发布。
whenOtherWins_en: If categories are highly balanced and you only want a quick sanity check (not a formal gate), raw percent is a fine glance — but never a release-blocking metric.
optionExplanations: 数值好看恰恰是虚高陷阱:不均衡类别的高一致率是随机赚来的,不是真可靠。
kappa 的公式里额外减掉了瞎蒙也能对的那部分,所以结论可能和百分比不一样,并不是同一套东西改个写法。
accuracy 需要 ground truth 真值,而 IAA 衡量的是标注者之间的一致,没有真值可比。
对;这道减法保住了 kappa 在类别失衡时依然可信的特性,这正是它被选中的原因。
optionExplanations_en: A good-looking number is exactly the inflation trap: high agreement on imbalanced categories is earned by chance, not reliability.
Kappa's formula additionally removes the share you'd get right by blind guessing, so its verdict can differ from raw percent — it isn't the same number in disguise.
Accuracy needs a ground-truth answer, but IAA measures agreement between annotators where no truth exists to compare against.
Correct — that subtraction is exactly what keeps kappa trustworthy when categories are skewed, which is why it's the right pick here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多标注者一致性指标,扣除随机一致后的真实一致程度,0-1 越高越一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fleiss' kappa is a multi-annotator agreement metric giving chance-corrected consistency on a 0-1 scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一种 chance-corrected 一致性指标,能处理缺失标注和多种标签类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Krippendorff's alpha is another chance-corrected agreement metric that handles missing labels and various label types.

scenario: 某仇恨言论类别的 Fleiss' kappa 实测只有 0.55。
scenario_en: A hate-speech category measures a Fleiss' kappa of only 0.55.
q: kappa ≈ 0.55(低于 0.6-0.7 的经验门槛)在设计上意味着什么动作？
q_en: What design action follows from kappa ≈ 0.55, below the 0.6-0.7 empirical gate?
why: kappa 门槛是经验质量闸门(rule of thumb):>0.8 很强、0.6-0.8 尚可、<0.6 偏弱。0.55 说明标注指南本身有歧义,该先修订指南再重标,而不是拿这批标签训练。
why_en: The kappa gate is an empirical rule of thumb (not derived): >0.8 strong, 0.6-0.8 acceptable, <0.6 weak; 0.55 says the guidelines themselves are ambiguous, so revise and re-annotate before training.
options: 0.55 说明模型不够大,加参数就能把一致性提上去
低于经验闸门:指南有歧义,先修订+重标,别用这批标签训练
0.55 只是随机波动,直接忽略、照常发布即可
0.55 说明该换个数值更高的指标(如原始百分比)来汇报
options_en: 0.55 means the model is too small; adding parameters will raise agreement.
Below the empirical gate: the guidelines are ambiguous, so revise and re-annotate before training on these labels.
0.55 is just random noise; ignore it and ship as usual.
0.55 means you should switch to a higher-scoring metric (like raw percent) for reporting.

termDefinitions.term: kappa gate / kappa 质量闸门
termDefinitions.meaning: 用 kappa 阈值(经验值:<0.6 偏弱)决定这批标注能不能进训练的质量卡点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A kappa gate uses a kappa threshold (rule of thumb: <0.6 is weak) to decide whether a batch of labels may enter training.

optionExplanations: 把差距归给模型容量是找错了层——kappa 量的是标注者之间的一致,加参数救不了指南本身的歧义。
对;0.55 已经跌破经验闸门下限,根因通常是指南对边界案例交代不清,该先补规则再重标,不能直接拿去训练。
当噪声当波动忽略,劣质标签会原样进模型,不是可以照常发布的小事。
换个更宽松的指标只是让数字好看,标注本身的歧义没被解决,反而把问题藏起来。
optionExplanations_en: Blaming model capacity targets the wrong layer — kappa measures agreement between annotators, and more parameters can't fix ambiguous guidelines.
Correct — 0.55 is already below the empirical gate, usually because the guidelines leave borderline cases unclear; revise them and re-annotate before training.
Treating it as random noise lets the noisy labels flow into training unchanged — not a minor thing to shrug off.
Switching to a looser metric just makes the number look better; the underlying annotation ambiguity is still there, only hidden.

scenario: 仇恨言论类别目标 kappa≥0.70,实测只有 0.55,明显没过闸门。
scenario_en: Hate speech targets kappa≥0.70 but measures 0.55, clearly failing the gate.
q: kappa 没达标时,最该采取哪个动作？
q_en: When kappa falls short, what is the right action to take?
why: 修订标注指南、补更清晰的边界样例(讽刺 vs 仇恨、counter-speech 的界线),然后重标。低 kappa 的根因是指南歧义,不是标注者不努力;调低目标或换指标都是掩盖问题、把噪声灌进 reward。
why_en: Revise the annotation guidelines with clearer borderline examples and re-annotate, because low kappa signals guideline ambiguity, not lazy annotators.
tradeoff: 修订指南+重标(治本但慢) vs 调低目标/换指标(快但掩盖歧义、噪声进模型)
options: 把目标 kappa 从 0.70 下调到 0.55,让它'达标'
改用原始百分比一致率汇报,数值高一些就算过
修订标注指南、补清晰的边界样例,然后重新标注
无视一致性,直接拿现有标签训练,反正样本量够大
options_en: Lower the target kappa from 0.70 to 0.55 so it 'passes.'
Switch reporting to raw percent agreement; a higher number counts as passing.
Revise the annotation guidelines with clearer borderline examples, then re-annotate.
Ignore agreement and train on the existing labels anyway since the sample size is large.
whenOtherWins: 若是像 misinformation 这类目标本就低(≥0.60)、分歧被视为正常的类别,可以接受分歧、把样本路由到 fact-check,而不是死磕重标到高 kappa。
whenOtherWins_en: For a category like misinformation where the target is intentionally low (≥0.60) and disagreement is expected, accept it and route to fact-check rather than forcing re-annotation to a high kappa.
optionExplanations: 下调目标是自欺:门槛为了守住可靠度,挪门槛不解决指南歧义,标签照样噪声。
换成会虚高的指标是掩盖问题,等于把不可靠标注洗白后灌进模型。
对;低 kappa 的根因在指南,补边界样例+重标才是治本动作。
样本量大掩盖不了系统性歧义,量越大只会把不一致放得越大。
optionExplanations_en: Lowering the target is self-deception: the gate exists to protect reliability, and moving it doesn't fix guideline ambiguity — labels stay noisy.
Switching to an inflating metric masks the problem, laundering unreliable labels into the model.
Correct — low kappa is rooted in the guidelines, so clarifying borderline examples and re-annotating is the fix at the source.
A large sample can't hide systematic ambiguity; more volume just amplifies the inconsistency.

scenario: 某类别 kappa 怎么都上不去,有人提议:干脆改用原始百分比一致率来汇报,数字立刻就'好看'了。
scenario_en: A category's kappa won't budge, so someone proposes switching to raw percent agreement, which instantly looks 'better.'
q: 把 kappa 偷换成原始百分比来'提高'一致性分数,会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you swap kappa for raw percent agreement to 'boost' the consistency score?
why: 原始百分比在类别不均衡时会虚高(safe 占绝大多数,瞎标也高一致),于是分数变好看→掩盖了指南歧义这个真问题→劣质标签照进训练→模型在违规类上悄悄退化。这是典型反模式,治标不治本。
why_en: Raw percent inflates on imbalanced categories, so the score looks better while masking the real guideline ambiguity, letting bad labels into training and quietly degrading the model on violations.
options: 没有副作用,只是换成一个更直观、更好解释的指标而已
会真的提高标注一致性,因为百分比更严格
百分比在不均衡类别虚高→掩盖指南歧义→劣质标签进训练
只影响对外汇报口径,不影响真正进入训练的标签质量
options_en: No side effect — it just swaps in a metric that's more intuitive and easier to explain.
It genuinely raises annotation consistency because percent is stricter.
Percent inflates on imbalanced categories → masks guideline ambiguity → bad labels enter training.
It only changes the external reporting convention, not the quality of labels entering training.
optionExplanations: 换指标不改变标注本身,只是把不可靠度藏起来,副作用恰恰在下游。
百分比更宽松而非更严格,不均衡时它系统性高估,不会真的提高一致性。
对;虚高分数掩盖歧义,劣质标签一路进模型,违规召回悄悄塌陷。
汇报口径的偏差会直接影响'这批能不能用'的判断,进而影响进训练的标签。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping metrics doesn't change the labels; it just hides the unreliability, with the damage downstream.
Percent is looser, not stricter; under imbalance it systematically overestimates and won't truly raise consistency.
Correct — the inflated score masks ambiguity, bad labels flow into the model, and violation recall quietly collapses.
A biased reporting convention drives the 'is this batch usable' call and thus the labels that enter training.

scenario: 一批样本标注者分歧很大(5 人里 3:2 分裂),有人想强制多数投票、给每条定一个硬标签就了事。
scenario_en: A batch has high disagreement (5 annotators split 3:2), and someone wants to force a majority vote and assign each a hard label.
q: 对高分歧样本,强制多数投票 vs 别的做法,哪个更对？
q_en: For high-disagreement items, is forcing a majority vote right, or something else?
why: 分歧本身是有价值的信号:高分歧=内容本就模糊。强制多数投票把这个信息抹掉了。更好的做法是路由到裁决流程,并把'标注者分歧程度'当成一个辅助 MTL 目标去预测,提升模型在边界内容上的校准。
why_en: Disagreement is itself signal — high disagreement means the item is genuinely ambiguous — so route it to adjudication and model disagreement as an auxiliary MTL target rather than crushing it into a majority vote.
tradeoff: 保留分歧+路由裁决(留住模糊信号) vs 强制多数投票(简单但抹掉信息、坑掉校准)
options: 保留分歧、路由裁决,并把分歧程度当辅助 MTL 目标预测
强制多数投票,3:2 就按 3 那边定硬标签,简单快速
直接丢掉所有高分歧样本,只留一致的干净样本训练
把分歧样本随机指派一个标签,反正模型会平均掉噪声
options_en: Keep the disagreement, route it to adjudication, and model disagreement as an auxiliary MTL target.
Force a majority vote — 3:2 becomes a hard label on the 3 side — simple and fast.
Drop all high-disagreement items and train only on the clean, agreed ones.
Randomly assign a label to disagreement items since the model averages out noise anyway.
whenOtherWins: 若某条分歧其实源于个别标注者的手误/走神(而非内容真模糊),那多数投票纠错就够,不必升级裁决。
whenOtherWins_en: If a disagreement stems from one annotator's slip rather than genuine ambiguity, a majority vote to correct it is enough without escalating to adjudication.
optionExplanations: 对;分歧=模糊信号,留住它并预测分歧程度,能让模型对边界内容更诚实。
多数投票把 3:2 的模糊硬压成 1,丢掉的正是最该学的边界信息。
丢掉高分歧样本=只在容易的样本上训练,模型遇到真正难的边界就崩。
随机指派是往标签里注入纯噪声,不会被'平均掉',只会拉低校准。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — disagreement is an ambiguity signal; keeping it and predicting the disagreement level makes the model more honest on borderline content.
A majority vote crushes a 3:2 ambiguity into a 1, discarding exactly the borderline information most worth learning.
Dropping high-disagreement items trains only on easy cases, so the model breaks on the genuinely hard borderline.
Random assignment injects pure noise into labels; it isn't 'averaged out' and only worsens calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务学习:一个模型同时学多个相关目标,这里把'预测标注分歧'当辅助任务提升主任务校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTL (Multi-Task Learning) trains one model on several related objectives at once, here using 'predict annotator disagreement' as an auxiliary task.

scenario: 分歧超过阈值的样本要人来定夺,但政策专家时间极贵,不可能每条模糊内容都让专家看。
scenario_en: Items with above-threshold disagreement need human adjudication, but policy experts are very expensive and can't review every ambiguous item.
q: 怎么组织人工裁决,既保证质量又省专家时间？
q_en: How do you organize adjudication to protect quality while sparing expert time?
why: 用多层裁决金字塔:众包标注者 → 训练过的专员 → 政策专家,分歧越大才越往上升级。这样把昂贵的专家时间集中在最难的那一小撮内容上,大多数在下层就解决了。
why_en: Use a multi-tier adjudication pyramid — crowd annotators → trained specialists → policy experts — escalating only the hardest items so expensive expert time is concentrated where it matters.
tradeoff: 多层金字塔(专家只看最难、成本可控) vs 全部送专家(质量高但成本不可持续)
diagram:
flowchart TB
  A["分歧超阈值的样本"] --> B["众包标注者"]
  B -->|仍分歧| C["训练过的专员"]
  C -->|仍分歧| D["政策专家"]
  D --> E["最终裁定"]
options: 所有模糊内容一律直接送政策专家,保证最高质量
多层金字塔:众包→专员→政策专家,分歧越大越往上升级
模糊内容一律交给模型自己定,不引入人工裁决
按提交时间排队,先到先由专家处理,不分难易
options_en: Send all ambiguous content straight to policy experts for the highest quality.
A multi-tier pyramid — crowd, then specialists, then policy experts — escalating as disagreement grows.
Let the model decide all ambiguous content itself with no human adjudication.
Queue by submission time so experts handle first-come-first-served regardless of difficulty.
whenOtherWins: 若某类违规极高危(如 child safety),哪怕量大也可能要求跳过下层、直接上专家/双专家复核,这时'全部送专家'反而是对的。
whenOtherWins_en: For an extreme-risk category like child safety, you may require skipping lower tiers and going straight to expert (or dual-expert) review, making 'all to experts' the right call there.
optionExplanations: 全送专家质量最高但成本不可持续,专家会被简单模糊件淹没,产能崩掉。
对;金字塔按难度分流,专家时间集中在最难件,是质量与成本的平衡解。
模糊件恰恰是模型最不该单独决定的,那正是需要人工的地方。
按时间排队不看难易,专家照样被简单件占满,没解决成本问题。
optionExplanations_en: All-to-experts is highest quality but unsustainable; experts drown in easy ambiguous items and throughput collapses.
Correct — the pyramid routes by difficulty, concentrating expert time on the hardest items, balancing quality and cost.
Ambiguous items are exactly what the model shouldn't decide alone; that's precisely where humans are needed.
Time-ordered queuing ignores difficulty, so experts still fill up on easy items and the cost problem remains.

scenario: 一条边界内容,5 个标注者里 3 个判违规、2 个判安全。
scenario_en: For a borderline item, 3 of 5 annotators judge it violating and 2 judge it safe.
q: 该给这条样本什么样的训练标签？
q_en: What kind of training label should this item get?
why: 用 soft label:记录完整投票分布,目标设成 0.6(3/5)而不是硬 1/0。配交叉熵训练,模型学出来的置信度就是良好校准的——它输出的 0.6 真的对应'六成概率违规',而不是虚高的 1.0。
why_en: Use a soft label: record the full vote distribution as a 0.6 target (3/5), not a hard 1/0, so cross-entropy training yields well-calibrated confidence.
tradeoff: soft label(保留投票分布、校准好) vs 硬标签(简单但丢分布、置信度虚高)
options: 硬标签 1(违规),因为多数判违规,少数服从多数是最省事的口径
硬标签 0(安全),存疑从宽,避免误删
soft label:目标设成 0.6(完整投票分布),配交叉熵训练
干脆丢掉这条样本,只用全票一致的样本训练
options_en: Hard label 1 (violating), since the majority judged it violating and majority rule is the simplest convention.
Hard label 0 (safe), giving benefit of the doubt to avoid false removals.
Soft label: set the target to 0.6, the full vote distribution, and train with cross-entropy.
Just drop this item and train only on unanimous ones.
whenOtherWins: 若这类内容最终要做二元自动处置(如 child safety 必须给出删/不删),仍可在 soft label 之上卡一个硬阈值,但训练标签本身用 soft 的更能校准。
whenOtherWins_en: If the content ultimately needs a binary auto-decision (child safety must remove or not), you can still threshold on top of the soft label, but the training target itself is better kept soft.
optionExplanations: 硬 1 把 3:2 的模糊说成板上钉钉,训练出过度自信、校准差的模型。
硬 0 同理只是反方向,一样抹掉了投票分布里的不确定性。
对;soft label 保留分布,交叉熵让输出概率对齐真实模糊度,置信度可信可用于路由。
丢掉边界样本=只学容易的,模型在最需要判断的模糊区反而没训练。
optionExplanations_en: Hard 1 turns a 3:2 ambiguity into certainty, training an overconfident, poorly calibrated model.
Hard 0 is the same mistake in the other direction, erasing the uncertainty in the vote distribution.
Correct — a soft label preserves the distribution, and cross-entropy aligns output probability with true ambiguity, giving trustworthy confidence for routing.
Dropping borderline items trains only on the easy ones, leaving the model untrained on the very region that needs judgment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用完整投票分布(如 0.6)当训练目标,而不是硬 1/0,保留标注不确定性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A soft label uses the full vote distribution (e.g. 0.6) as the training target instead of a hard 1/0, preserving annotation uncertainty.

scenario: 你想让系统自己知道'这条内容有多模糊',好把真正模糊的路由给人、把清楚的自动处置。
scenario_en: You want the system to know how ambiguous an item is, so genuinely ambiguous ones go to humans and clear ones are auto-decided.
q: 怎么让模型学会预测'内容的模糊程度',并用它做路由？
q_en: How do you make the model predict an item's ambiguity and use it for routing?
why: 把标注者分歧当成一个辅助预测目标:模型除了预测违规与否,还专门预测'这条会不会引起标注分歧'。模型预测出高模糊度 → confidence-based routing 就把它送到人工,而不是让自动决策去处理边界内容。
why_en: Make annotator disagreement an auxiliary prediction target so the model predicts ambiguity, then confidence-based routing sends high-ambiguity items to humans instead of automated decisions.
options: 把违规概率四舍五入成 0/1,就当作模糊度,不需要额外训练目标
只看模型 loss 大小当模糊度,loss 大就送人工
随机抽一部分内容送人工,不预测模糊度
把标注者分歧当辅助预测目标,高模糊度经 confidence 路由人工
options_en: Round the violation probability to 0/1 and call that ambiguity, so no extra training target is needed.
Use the training loss magnitude as ambiguity — large loss means send to humans.
Randomly sample some content to humans without predicting ambiguity.
Make annotator disagreement an auxiliary prediction target; high predicted ambiguity routes the item to humans.
optionExplanations: 四舍五入把模糊度信息直接扔了,0/1 里根本没有'有多模糊'这一维。
训练 loss 是训练期的量、且受多因素干扰,不能在线当每条内容的模糊度用。
随机抽样不区分难易,把预算浪费在简单件上,真正模糊的照样漏。
对;显式学分歧当辅助目标,再用预测的模糊度驱动路由,边界内容才可靠地到人手里。
optionExplanations_en: Rounding throws away the ambiguity information; a 0/1 has no 'how ambiguous' dimension at all.
Training loss is a train-time quantity confounded by many factors and can't serve as per-item online ambiguity.
Random sampling ignores difficulty, wastes budget on easy items, and still misses the genuinely ambiguous ones.
Correct — explicitly learning disagreement as an auxiliary target and routing on predicted ambiguity reliably gets borderline content to humans.

scenario: 团队发现:改善边界内容的处理,对整体执法一致性的提升,远大于同样精力花在清晰内容上。
scenario_en: The team finds that improving borderline handling lifts overall enforcement consistency far more than the same effort spent on clear content.
q: 为什么 borderline 内容的处理对 enforcement consistency 影响这么大？
q_en: Why does borderline handling have such an outsized effect on enforcement consistency?
why: 边界内容正是 predictive multiplicity 最高的地方——多个同样合理的模型会给出不同判定。所以这一小撮内容不成比例地驱动申诉和争议,把它处理好(soft label、路由人工)对执法一致性有超额影响。
why_en: Borderline items are where predictive multiplicity is highest — equally plausible models disagree — so this small slice disproportionately drives appeals and controversy, giving better handling outsized impact.
options: 因为边界内容 predictive multiplicity 最高,争议集中在此
因为边界内容数量最多,占平台每天绝大部分流量,规模上压倒其他所有类别
因为边界内容都是明显违规,处理它们最省事
因为边界内容和一致性无关,只是碰巧被提及
options_en: Because borderline items are where predictive multiplicity is highest, so appeals and controversy concentrate there.
Because borderline items are the most numerous, making up most of the platform's daily traffic and dwarfing every other category.
Because borderline items are all clearly violating, making them the easiest to handle.
Because borderline items are unrelated to consistency and just happen to be mentioned.
optionExplanations: 对;多个合理模型在边界处分歧最大,这一小撮驱动了大部分申诉,改善它回报最高。
边界内容其实是少数,大部分内容清晰安全或明显违规,不是量最多。
边界内容恰恰是不明显的那类,说它'明显违规'与定义矛盾。
边界处理与一致性强相关,不是无关顺带一提。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — equally plausible models disagree most at the border, and this small slice drives most appeals, so improving it has the highest payoff.
Borderline content is actually a minority; most content is clearly safe or clearly violating, not the largest share.
Borderline content is precisely the non-obvious kind, so calling it 'clearly violating' contradicts the definition.
Borderline handling is strongly tied to consistency, not an unrelated aside.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个精度相当的模型对同一样本给出不同预测的现象,在边界内容上最严重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predictive multiplicity is when several equally accurate models give different predictions for the same item, worst on borderline content.

scenario: 政策每周变、新违规类型(深伪、编码仇恨)不断冒头,静态训练集几周就过时;标注预算有限,只能标一小部分。
scenario_en: Policies change weekly and new violation types (deepfakes, coded hate) keep emerging, staling a static set within weeks, while the labeling budget covers only a small fraction.
q: 该怎么挑选样本送人工标注,才最划算？
q_en: How should you pick items for human labeling to get the most value?
why: 用 uncertainty sampling:让生产模型给每条内容打分,优先把接近决策边界/预测熵最大的样本送人工。这形成正向飞轮——人标最难的 → 重训后在前沿更强 → 又surface下一批最难的,标注花在最有信息量的样本上。
why_en: Use uncertainty sampling: score every item with the production model and prioritize those near the decision boundary or at max prediction entropy, forming a flywheel that spends labels on the most informative items.
tradeoff: uncertainty sampling(标最难/信息量最大) vs 随机采样(简单但大量标到已会的简单件)
options: 随机均匀采样,保证各类内容都被覆盖到,简单又公平
只标模型最有把握的高置信样本,先把简单干净的那批全标完再谈难例
uncertainty sampling:优先标决策边界/最高熵的样本
只标最老的样本,先把历史积压清干净再谈新数据
options_en: Random uniform sampling so every content type gets covered — simple and fair.
Label only the highest-confidence items, finishing the whole easy clean batch before touching hard cases.
Uncertainty sampling: prioritize items near the decision boundary or with the highest entropy.
Label only the oldest items, clearing the historical backlog before touching new data.
whenOtherWins: 冷启动、还没有可信生产模型可打分时,用随机/分层采样先播下第一批标签,等模型能给出可信不确定度后再切到 uncertainty sampling。
whenOtherWins_en: At cold start with no trustworthy model to score, seed the first labels with random/stratified sampling, then switch to uncertainty sampling once the model gives reliable uncertainty.
optionExplanations: 随机采样大量落在模型已会的简单件上,对稀有违规的学习效率极低。
标高置信件模型本来就会,几乎学不到新东西,信息量最低。
对;优先标边界/高熵样本,把有限标注花在模型最不确定处,飞轮越转越强。
按时间清积压不看信息量,老样本可能全是简单件,浪费预算。
optionExplanations_en: Random sampling lands mostly on easy items the model already knows, giving very low efficiency for rare violations.
Labeling high-confidence items teaches almost nothing since the model already knows them — lowest information.
Correct — prioritizing boundary/high-entropy items spends limited labels where the model is most uncertain, and the flywheel compounds.
Clearing backlog by age ignores information value; old items may all be easy, wasting the budget.

termDefinitions.term: uncertainty sampling / 不确定性采样
termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型给全量数据打分,优先把最不确定(接近边界/熵最大)的样本送人工标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Uncertainty sampling scores all data and prioritizes the most uncertain items (near the boundary / max entropy) for human labeling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出概率分布的熵,越接近均匀(如 0.5/0.5)越不确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prediction entropy is the entropy of the model's output distribution; closer to uniform (e.g. 0.5/0.5) means more uncertain.

scenario: 对稀有违规类别,uncertainty sampling 在标签效率上比随机采样高 2-5 倍。
scenario_en: For rare violation categories, uncertainty sampling is 2-5x more label-efficient than random sampling.
q: 这个 2-5x 的数字对设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this 2-5x figure imply for design?
why: 2-5x 是经验量级(非公式推导):同等模型质量下,uncertainty sampling 约只需随机采样 1/5-1/2 的标注量,因为随机在稀有违规上大多标到简单负样本上。
why_en: The 2-5x figure is an empirical order of magnitude, not derived: reaching the same quality needs roughly a fifth to a half of the labels, since random sampling wastes most of its budget on easy negatives for rare violations.
options: 说明主动学习纯属噱头,随机采样一样好,不值得搭基础设施
说明只要标注量翻倍,任何采样都能达到同样效果
约 1/5-1/2 标注量就够:主动挑边界样本把预算花在刀刃上
说明标签越多模型一定越好、没有上限,堆量即可
options_en: It shows active learning is a gimmick and random is just as good, not worth the infrastructure.
It shows that doubling label volume makes any sampling reach the same result.
Roughly 1/5 to 1/2 the labels suffice, because uncertainty sampling spends the budget where it counts.
It shows more labels always mean a better model with no ceiling; just pile on volume.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达到某模型质量所需的标注数量,越少越高效;主动学习在稀有类上更高效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label efficiency is how few labels are needed to reach a given model quality; active learning is more efficient on rare classes.

optionExplanations: 把这当成噱头忽略了根本问题——随机采样在稀有类别上大多标到容易的负样本,白白浪费预算。
标注量翻倍不会自动修正采样策略选错的问题,浪费的预算依旧浪费在同一批简单样本上。
对;同等质量只需约 1/5-1/2 的标注量,这足以证明为它多搭一套打分+路由基础设施是划算的。
标签数量不是无上限地兑换质量,采样策略选对了,少量标注就能顶多量随机标注。
optionExplanations_en: Dismissing it as a gimmick misses the core issue — random sampling on rare categories mostly labels easy negatives, wasting the budget.
Doubling label volume doesn't fix a bad sampling choice; the extra budget still gets spent on the same easy items.
Correct — reaching the same quality with roughly 1/5-1/2 the labels is enough to justify building the extra scoring + routing infrastructure.
Label count isn't an unlimited trade for quality; with the right sampling strategy, fewer labels can beat a much larger random batch.

q: 把内容审核的主动学习飞轮排成正确的循环顺序:
q_en: Order the content-moderation active-learning flywheel correctly:
steps: 生产模型给每条内容打分,给出校准过的置信度
把最不确定(接近边界/最高熵)的样本 surface 给人工
人工按政策 taxonomy 标注,IAA 保证质量
用新标签增量重训,模型在原本吃力的样例上变强
重训后的模型 surface 出新一批不确定样本,进入下一轮
why: 闭环:模型打分 → 不确定样本路由人工 → 人工标注 → 增量重训 → 新前沿再 surface 出难样本。每转一圈,模型在前沿变强、又暴露下一批最难的,标注预算始终花在最有信息量处。
why_en: The loop: model scores, uncertain items route to humans, humans label, incremental retrain, and the new frontier surfaces fresh hard items — each turn strengthening the model where it's weakest.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模型打分
校准置信度"] --> B["路由最不确定样本"] B --> C["人工标注
IAA 质量"] C --> D["增量重训"] D --> E["新不确定前沿"] E --> A

termDefinitions.term: policy taxonomy / 政策分类体系
termDefinitions.meaning: 把违规类型组织成层级类目(仇恨/暴力/裸露…),标注和处置都对齐这套体系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A policy taxonomy organizes violation types into a hierarchy (hate/violence/nudity...) that labeling and enforcement both align to.

scenario: 平台每天数十亿条内容,人工复审产能有限,得定一个'送多少去人工'的采样预算。
scenario_en: The platform sees billions of items daily with limited human-review capacity, so you must set a sampling budget of how much goes to human review.
q: 送人工复审的采样预算大致怎么定？
q_en: How is the human-review sampling budget roughly set?
why: 经验预算约每天总量的 0.1-1%,按类别分别定(不是公式,是产能/成本目标)。它直接决定要配多少审核人力,也框定了主动学习每轮能标多少。child safety 是例外——不受这个预算限制,一律人工复审。
why_en: An empirical budget of roughly 0.1-1% of daily volume, set per category (a capacity/cost target, not a formula), which sizes reviewer headcount — with child safety exempt and always reviewed.
options: 把当天 100% 内容都送人工复审,确保零漏检
固定送 50%,一半自动一半人工,简单好记
完全不设预算,模型不确定多少就送多少,不设上限也不看人力产能
约每天总量 0.1-1%,按类别分定,child safety 例外
options_en: Send 100% of the day's content to human review to guarantee zero misses.
Fix it at 50% — half automated, half human — simple to remember.
Set no budget at all — send however many the model is uncertain about, uncapped and ignoring reviewer capacity.
Roughly 0.1-1% of daily volume, set per category, with child safety exempt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每天送人工复审的内容占总量的比例上限,由审核产能和成本决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sampling budget is the cap on the share of daily content sent to human review, set by reviewer capacity and cost.

optionExplanations: 把全部内容都送人工在数十亿量级下产能会直接崩溃,也把预算浪费在明显安全的内容上。
固定比例不看类别风险和产能现实,高危类别按 50% 抽审不够严,低危类别又浪费人力。
不设上限会让审核产能被不确定性最高的一批样本无限占用,团队排不出班表。
对;预算按产能和成本定在千分之一到百分之一量级,child safety 单独例外不受限。
optionExplanations_en: Sending everything to humans collapses reviewer capacity at billions-per-day scale and wastes effort on obviously safe content.
A fixed percentage ignores per-category risk and capacity — too loose for high-stakes categories, wasteful for low-stakes ones.
With no cap, review capacity gets consumed without limit by whichever batch looks most uncertain, and staffing can't be planned.
Correct — the budget is set at roughly a tenth to one percent of volume by capacity and cost, with child safety exempt from the cap.

scenario: 两类内容:child safety 和 spam,模型对两者都给出很高的置信度。
scenario_en: Two categories, child safety and spam, both scored with high model confidence.
q: 高置信度就能一律走自动处置吗？不同类别该怎么分层？
q_en: Does high confidence mean auto-decide for all? How should categories be stratified?
why: 不能一刀切。child safety 因为漏放代价极端不对称,无论置信度多高都强制人工复审;spam 之类可以按不确定度走自动化。分层依据是每类的非对称成本,而不是单看置信度高低。
why_en: No — child safety has extreme asymmetric cost, so it's human-reviewed regardless of confidence, while spam-like categories can follow uncertainty-based automation; stratify by per-category asymmetric cost.
tradeoff: 按类别非对称成本分层(child safety 必审) vs 一律按置信度自动(漏放高危代价不可接受)
options: child safety 无论置信度多高都强制人工(极端非对称成本)
只要置信度高,所有类别一律自动处置,包括 child safety
所有类别一律人工复审,不管什么内容都不自动
按内容长度分层,长的送人工、短的自动
options_en: Child safety stays human-reviewed regardless of confidence, because the cost is extremely asymmetric.
As long as confidence is high, auto-decide all categories including child safety.
Human-review every category always, never automating anything.
Stratify by content length — long to humans, short automated.
whenOtherWins: 对 spam 这类漏一条代价极低的类别,高置信度直接自动处置是对的,没必要占用宝贵人工产能。
whenOtherWins_en: For low-stakes categories like spam where a miss costs little, high-confidence auto-decisions are correct and needn't consume scarce human capacity.
optionExplanations: 对;分层的依据是非对称成本,child safety 漏放代价极高必须必审,其余按不确定度。
对 child safety 一律信任模型置信度=把极端高危交给可能出错的自动决策,不可接受。
全人工审在数十亿量级下产能崩溃,也浪费在明显安全内容上。
内容长度和危害严重度无关,不是合理的分层依据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — stratify by asymmetric cost: child safety's miss cost is extreme so it's always reviewed, others follow uncertainty.
Trusting model confidence for child safety hands an extreme-risk category to fallible automation — unacceptable.
Reviewing everything by hand collapses under billions and wastes effort on clearly safe content.
Content length is unrelated to harm severity and isn't a sound basis for stratification.

scenario: 政策每周变、新违规类型不断冒头,训练集会 stale;要定 retraining 的节奏。
scenario_en: With weekly policy changes and emerging violation types staling the training set, you must set the retraining cadence.
q: 面对快速演进的政策,retraining 节奏大致怎么排？
q_en: Against fast-evolving policy, how is the retraining cadence roughly scheduled?
why: 分两档:增量微调按天/周做(快速吸收新标签、追上新违规),全量重训按月做(周期性重建、防漂移累积)。这些是由政策演进速度驱动的节奏目标,不是公式;政策变得越快,增量微调就要越勤。
why_en: Two tiers: incremental fine-tuning daily/weekly to absorb new labels, and full retraining monthly to rebuild periodically — cadence targets driven by how fast policy evolves, not a formula.
options: 只在模型明显崩掉时才重训一次,平时完全不动
增量微调按天/周,全量重训按月,节奏由政策演进速度驱动
每小时全量重训一次,越频繁越好,不计成本
训练一次就永久部署,政策变化全靠规则后处理硬扛
options_en: Retrain only once when the model visibly breaks, otherwise never touch it.
Incremental fine-tuning daily or weekly and a full retrain monthly, paced by how fast policy evolves.
Full retrain every hour — the more often the better, regardless of cost.
Train once and deploy forever, absorbing every policy change with rule-based post-processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练数据从'新鲜'到'跟不上当前政策/违规'之间的时间跨度,决定重训频率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A staleness window is how long training data stays current before falling behind policy/violations, setting the retraining frequency.

optionExplanations: 只在崩溃后才补救属于事后救火,政策每周都在变,等模型明显跟不上时申诉早已堆积。
对;增量微调按天/周吸收新标签,全量重训按月防漂移,节奏跟着政策演进速度走。
每小时重训一次的成本远超收益,数据和评估都来不及积累,纯粹烧算力。
训练一次就不再更新,遇到政策每周变、新违规类型冒头时,规则补丁永远追不上模型本身该学的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining only after a visible breakdown is pure firefighting; with weekly policy changes, appeals pile up long before the model looks obviously wrong.
Correct — incremental fine-tuning daily/weekly absorbs new labels while monthly full retraining guards against drift, pacing with how fast policy moves.
Retraining every hour burns far more compute than it buys; there isn't even enough new data or evaluation time between runs to justify it.
Training once and freezing the model can't keep up with weekly policy shifts and new violation types no rule patch can fully cover.

scenario: 一个刚重训好的模型准备上线,直接拿它的置信度去驱动'哪些送人工'的路由,没先验证校准。
scenario_en: A freshly retrained model is about to ship, driving the 'what goes to humans' routing with its confidence, without first validating calibration.
q: 为什么必须先在留出集上验证校准再上线？跳过会怎样？
q_en: Why validate calibration on a held-out set before shipping, and what if you skip it?
why: 路由完全依赖置信度的可信度。校准差 → 模型说的 0.5 其实不是真 0.5 → 路由把错的内容送人工(简单件占满产能、真难的反而被自动误判)→ 飞轮空转甚至倒转、审核质量下滑。所以要在留出校准集上验证后再上线。
why_en: Routing depends on confidence being trustworthy, so poor calibration sends the wrong items to humans — clogging capacity with easy cases while hard ones get auto-misjudged — breaking the flywheel, which is why you validate on a held-out set first.
options: 校准无所谓,只要模型准确率高,置信度数值随便都行
跳过验证只是省点时间,对路由和飞轮没有影响
校准差→路由送错内容→飞轮空转、质量下滑;须先在留出集验证
校准只影响训练收敛速度,和线上路由无关
options_en: Calibration doesn't matter; as long as accuracy is high, confidence values can be anything.
Skipping validation just saves time and has no effect on routing or the flywheel.
Poor calibration routes the wrong items, the flywheel stalls and quality drops — validate on a held-out set first.
Calibration only affects training convergence speed, unrelated to online routing.
optionExplanations: 准确率高但置信度不可信,照样把错的内容路由给人,校准是路由的前提。
跳过验证会让不可信的置信度直接驱动路由,后果全在下游,不是无痛。
对;校准是路由的命门,坏校准让飞轮把人力浪费在简单件、放过真难件,先验证再上线。
校准差影响的是线上置信度可信度和路由,不只是训练收敛。
optionExplanations_en: High accuracy with untrustworthy confidence still routes wrong items to humans; calibration is the precondition for routing.
Skipping validation lets untrustworthy confidence drive routing, with all consequences downstream — not painless.
Correct — calibration is the linchpin of routing; bad calibration wastes humans on easy items and lets hard ones through, so validate before shipping.
Poor calibration harms online confidence reliability and routing, not just training convergence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出的置信度与真实正确概率相符的程度;校准好时预测 0.7 就约七成正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is how well predicted confidence matches the true probability of being correct; well-calibrated 0.7 means about 70% correct.

scenario: 收尾:数据策略给下一课的架构铺好四块地基。
scenario_en: Wrap-up: the data strategy lays four foundations for the next lesson's architecture.
q: 补全内容审核数据策略的四大地基:
q_en: Fill in the four foundations of the content-moderation data strategy:
text: 四大地基:(1){{多模态}}信号采集,每个模态独立提取;(2)policy-aware 标注,配可测的 {{IAA}} 阈值;(3)borderline 处理靠 {{soft label}} + disagreement-as-feature;(4){{主动学习}}飞轮靠 uncertainty sampling。这里产出的 {{置信度}} 分数,就是下一课分层集成里的路由依据。
text_en: Four foundations: (1) {{multimodal}} signal collection with per-modality extraction; (2) policy-aware annotation with measurable {{IAA}} thresholds; (3) borderline handling via {{soft labels}} + disagreement-as-feature; (4) an {{active-learning}} flywheel via uncertainty sampling. The {{confidence}} scores produced here become the routing mechanism in the next lesson's tiered ensemble.
why: 四块地基环环相扣:信号采集给证据、标注质量设天花板、borderline 处理保校准、主动学习追上政策。它们共同产出可信的 confidence 分数,喂给下一课的分层集成做路由。
why_en: The four foundations interlock — signals, label quality, borderline handling, and active learning — jointly producing trustworthy confidence scores that feed the next lesson's tiered routing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标注者一致性,用 kappa/alpha 衡量,是标注质量闸门。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAA (Inter-Annotator Agreement) measures labeler consistency via kappa/alpha and gates label quality.

scenario: 这一课产出的是每条内容带校准的 confidence 分数;下一课要设计分层集成架构(快速 triage + 慢速高精度 borderline 分类器)。
scenario_en: This lesson outputs calibrated confidence per item; the next designs a tiered ensemble (fast triage + slow high-accuracy borderline classifier).
q: 数据策略里的 confidence 分数,在下一课的架构里主要扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role do the data-strategy confidence scores mainly play in the next lesson's architecture?
why: 它是分层路由的开关:高置信(明显安全/明显违规)由快速 triage 自动处置,不确定的才升级到慢速高精度 borderline 分类器和人工。数据策略先把置信度校准好,架构才能靠它省算力又不漏难件。
why_en: It's the tiered-routing switch: high-confidence items get automated by fast triage, and only uncertain ones escalate to the slow high-accuracy borderline classifier and humans.
tradeoff: 置信度驱动分层路由(省算力、只把难件上重模型) vs 全部走重模型(精度高但数十亿量级扛不住成本)
options: 只用来做离线报表和模型监控,和在线架构无关
决定用哪家云厂商部署模型和推理集群
决定视频编码格式与 CDN 节点位置,属于分发层
当分层路由的开关:高置信自动处置,不确定的升级人工
options_en: Only for offline reports and model monitoring, unrelated to the online architecture.
To decide which cloud vendor hosts the model and inference cluster.
To decide the video codec and CDN node placement, which is the delivery layer.
It's the tiered-routing switch: high confidence auto-decides, uncertain items escalate to humans.
whenOtherWins: 若内容量很小、算力充裕,可以让所有内容都走重模型、不做分层,这时 confidence 路由的省算力价值就不重要了。
whenOtherWins_en: If volume is tiny and compute is ample, you could run every item through the heavy model without tiering, making confidence routing's compute savings unimportant.
optionExplanations: confidence 是在线路由的核心信号,不是离线报表,低估了它的作用。
云厂商是部署选型,与 confidence 分数的路由用途无关。
编码/CDN 是分发层,与用置信度分层这件事无关。
对;校准好的置信度让架构把简单件低成本处置、把难件集中到重模型和人工,是分层的地基。
optionExplanations_en: Confidence is the core online routing signal, not an offline report — this underrates it.
Cloud vendor is a deployment choice, unrelated to the routing use of confidence scores.
Codec/CDN is the delivery layer, unrelated to tiering on confidence.
Correct — well-calibrated confidence lets the architecture cheaply auto-handle easy items and concentrate hard ones on the heavy model and humans, the basis of tiering.

scenario: Meta 级平台每天处理数十亿条跨模态内容。
scenario_en: A Meta-scale platform processes billions of cross-modal items daily.
q: '每天数十亿条'这个量级,对审核数据策略意味着什么？
q_en: What does the 'billions per day' scale imply for the moderation data strategy?
why: 数十亿/天是给定的产品规模:意味着人工审不完,自动化必须吃掉绝大多数,人工只留 0.1-1% 的最有价值样本,逼出主动学习+分层路由的设计。
why_en: Billions per day is a given product scale: humans can't review it all, so automation must handle the vast majority and humans get only the 0.1-1% most valuable items — which is exactly what forces active learning plus tiered routing.
options: 人工审不完:自动化吃绝大多数,人工只留 0.1-1% 最有价值样本
数十亿/天说明该雇足够多标注员把每条都人工审一遍
数十亿/天只是背景数字,对数据策略没有实际约束
数十亿/天说明该放弃 ML、全用固定规则匹配,规则最快
options_en: Humans can't review it all: automation handles the vast majority and humans get only the 0.1-1% most valuable items.
Billions/day means hire enough annotators to review every single item by hand.
Billions/day is just a background number with no real constraint on the data strategy.
Billions/day means drop ML and use fixed rule matching only, since rules are fastest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时含文本/图像/视频/音频多个模态的内容,是审核系统要统一处理的输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-modal content spans text/image/video/audio at once, the input a moderation system must handle uniformly.

optionExplanations: 对;数十亿/天这个规模逼出的是自动化为主、人工只挑最有价值样本的主动学习+分层路由设计。
雇再多标注员也追不上数十亿/天的量级,人力成本和产能天花板会先被打穿。
这个量级恰恰是设计的第一约束——它决定了人工审核不可能全覆盖,必须靠自动化和路由分流。
固定规则匹配不了政策每周变化、语义模糊的边界内容,规模再大也补不上判断力的缺口。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — billions per day is exactly the scale that forces an automation-first design with humans reserved for the most valuable items via active learning and tiered routing.
No amount of hiring keeps pace with billions per day; headcount cost and capacity hit a ceiling first.
This scale is precisely the first constraint on the design — it rules out full human coverage and forces automation plus routing.
Fixed rule matching can't track weekly policy changes or judge ambiguous borderline content, no matter how much scale you throw at it.

scenario: 同一张质量表里,child safety 目标 kappa≥0.85,而 misinformation 只要求≥0.60。
scenario_en: In the same quality table, child safety targets kappa≥0.85 while misinformation only requires ≥0.60.
q: 为什么不同违规类别的 kappa 目标不一样,而不是一个统一门槛？
q_en: Why are kappa targets category-specific rather than one universal threshold?
why: 门槛按非对称成本+固有模糊度定:child safety 漏放代价极端,要求近乎完美一致(≥0.85);misinformation 本就充满合理分歧,强求高 kappa 只会逼标注者硬凑(≥0.60 即可)。
why_en: Thresholds track each category's asymmetric cost and inherent ambiguity: child safety demands near-perfect agreement (≥0.85), while misinformation is inherently contestable so a high kappa would force artificial consensus.
options: 因为不同类别标注员人数不同,人多门槛就高
门槛按非对称成本+固有模糊度定:child safety 近乎完美
因为 child safety 的样本量更大,大样本自然 kappa 高
因为不同类别用不同语言标注,语言难度决定门槛
options_en: Because categories have different annotator counts, and more annotators means a higher bar.
Thresholds follow each category's asymmetric cost and inherent ambiguity — child safety needs near-perfect agreement.
Because child safety has larger sample sizes, and large samples naturally yield high kappa.
Because categories are labeled in different languages, and language difficulty sets the bar.
optionExplanations: 标注员人数不决定门槛,kappa 本身就是对多标注者算的一致性,人多不等于要求高。
对;门槛=该类别错误代价×固有可判定性,高危可判的要严,天生有争议的接受分歧。
样本量不改变 chance-corrected 的 kappa 期望,大样本只是让估计更稳,不抬门槛。
标注语言与门槛设定无关,门槛由危害成本和模糊度决定,不是语言难度。
optionExplanations_en: Annotator count doesn't set the bar; kappa is agreement computed across annotators, and more people doesn't mean a higher requirement.
Correct — the bar is error cost × inherent decidability: high-stakes decidable categories demand strictness, inherently contested ones accept disagreement.
Sample size doesn't change chance-corrected kappa's expectation; more data just stabilizes the estimate, not the bar.
Labeling language is unrelated to the threshold, which is set by harm cost and ambiguity, not language difficulty.
